items.note: Experiment with 82 participants on GenAI use in a creative task; outcomes are intrinsic motivation, self-assessed skills, and self-evaluated creative performance (title: self-perceived creativity), with no rated output reported in the abstract (abstract from the AIS eLibrary landing page).

Randomized classroom study in Ghana (ChatGPT vs databases and search engines for research-methods tasks); outcomes are the Critical, Creative, and Reflective Thinking Scales, which appear to be self-report instruments, and the task is not a creative task; next stage could confirm the scale type if in doubt.

CHI 2025 system paper (StoryPrompt) with a comparative evaluation of 40 children (grades 2-6) against a storyboard method, scoring storytelling creativity and richness; likely the same sample as c307 and below the 50-participant threshold.

Within-subjects experiment with 40 children comparing a GenAI storytelling system with a traditional storyboard, scoring creativity, richness, and coherence and reporting a narrowing of the quality gap; likely reanalysis of the same sample as c305 (StoryPrompt, CHI 2025); order randomization not stated; below 50 participants.

Pre-post study of collaborative digital mind-mapping with 163 students (28 with neurodevelopmental disorders) scored on the Torrance Figural test, with a comparison of AI-provided prompts vs none; unclear whether the AI prompts are generative AI and how the AI and non-AI groups were formed.

Quasi-experimental nonequivalent control group design with 50 fifth-graders: ChatGPT structured prompting vs conventional instruction for ethnoliteracy-based fiction writing, scored on a post-treatment writing test; unclear whether the test was written with AI available (with_ai) or without (after_ai).

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, Europe PMC); search notes describe a controlled design experiment comparing AIGC support, designer-designer collaboration, and image stimuli, with CPSS novelty and resolution ratings and cognitive load.

Turn-based collaborative storytelling with a human partner, an LLM partner, or two LLMs, measuring semantic novelty and narrative influence at the turn level; the human-human vs human-LLM contrast is an AI-assistance comparison, but outcomes are process measures of turns rather than rated creativity of final stories, and sample size is not stated.

Between-subjects online experiment (Indian and American participants) where all write with AI suggestions under no intervention or one of two value-framing interventions; outcomes are AI reliance and the uniqueness of final essays (homogenization, across_people); arXiv 2605.20512 is the same work as the FAccT 2026 paper.

Controlled 2x2 experiment in design education crossing generative AI tool type (text-to-image vs image-to-image) with figurative vs abstract visual stimuli, scoring design creativity in divergent and convergent stages; search notes report 84 students, which the abstract does not state.
